narrative:
On August 19, 2026, the Karnataka High Court recorded an overall hearing rate of 42.0%, hearing 1,179 of the 2,808 scheduled cases across 51 judges. This performance reflects steady operational throughput compared to recent sittings, closely aligning with the 43.3% rate (1,170 of 2,701 cases) on August 18 and 41.5% (1,301 of 3,134 cases) on August 17.

Workload and disposal rates varied significantly across benches. Justice S. Vishwajith Shetty managed the largest docket of 337 matters, hearing 118 cases (35.0%). Justice M. Nagaprasanna processed heavy cause lists effectively, taking up 100 of 154 scheduled matters (64.9%) in one roster alongside 29 of 50 (58.0%) in another. Justice V. Srishananda also posted robust progress, hearing 72 of 111 matters (64.9%). Conversely, certain rosters experienced lower conversion, such as Justice Hanchate Sanjeevkumar, who heard 11 of 86 cases (12.8%).

Stage-level clearance showed strong activity in interlocutory and preliminary stages, whereas substantive disposals lagged. Orders represented the highest stage volume, with 423 of 931 cases heard (45.4%), followed by Admission at 42.6% (192 of 451) and Preliminary Hearing at 44.4% (146 of 329). In contrast, Final Hearing matters converted at only 22.8% (148 of 649), continuing a downward trend from 27.0% on August 18 and 25.7% on August 17.

In terms of case types, Writ Petitions (WP) formed the largest portion of the docket with 1,255 listings, achieving a 38.6% hearing rate (484 heard), slightly lower than the 40.6% recorded the previous day. Criminal Petitions (CRL.P) achieved higher efficiency at 59.5% (204 of 343 heard), improving from 42.0% on August 18. Miscellaneous First Appeals (MFA) saw 155 of 403 cases heard (38.5%), while Regular Second Appeals (RSA) cleared 81 of 124 matters (65.3%). Civil Revision Petitions (CRP) had minimal movement, with only 2 of 58 matters heard (3.4%).
